questions.question: Can a caller receive bytes that are NOT the version they were verified against? (second read, re-open by path, cached buffer, path swap between digest and return, hardlinks, data non-None with a reason or non-verified status)
questions.answer: No, not through the handle's own version - the guarantee is genuine, and the only exception is the caller-supplied override parameter (finding B-VR03-01), which lets the caller redefine 'the version' and produces a result whose document_id and content_sha256 belong to different versions. Details: (i) NO second read and NO re-open by path: instrumentation counted exactly one open('rb') and two stat() calls per call, and nothing after the read touches the path except the stat; (ii) NO cached buffer: two consecutive calls after an on-disk overwrite returned the new on-disk bytes, i.e. every call re-reads; (iii) NO path swap between digest and return: the returned value is b''.join(chunks) built from the same chunk objects the digest consumed, after the comparison, with no path use in between; (iv) hardlink: a hardlink inside a root to a file outside is served with its real bytes, but realpath does not resolve hardlinks, so the bytes are still the requested version's bytes (a containment-semantics note, finding B-VR03-07, not a wrong-bytes path); (v) invariants: across 7 measured refusal kinds no result had data non-None, and no result had a non-empty reason with data, or data with a status other than 'verified'. The remaining fail-open discovered is cancellation (finding B-VR03-04): bytes can be returned while the budget is cancelled - but they ARE the verified version.
questions.evidence: RUN/evidence/b03_review_bytes.json scenarios happy_path (n_opens=1, n_stats=2), post_read_change_with_mtime_restored (bytes returned = requested version while the file on disk already held another version), caller_supplied_foreign_digest, refusal_invariants, cancel_inside_final_read

questions.question: Defeat the mid-read detection: is the size + mtime_ns re-check sufficient? same-size in-place overwrite; write with mtime restored via os.utime; write that lands between the last read() and the post-stat; truncate-and-rewrite to the same length; append that returns to the original size - does the entry point return bytes, and can those bytes differ from the requested version?
questions.answer: The size+mtime_ns re-check is NOT sufficient as a change detector - I defeated it in two of the five attacks - but defeating it never yields wrong bytes, because the digest comparison after it is what actually binds the returned buffer to the requested version. Per attack: (1) same-size in-place overwrite before the call -> no bytes, unavailable/content_sha256_mismatch. (2) same-size overwrite + os.utime restoring the original mtime_ns -> GUARD DEFEATED (measured: st_mtime_ns 1789251840518958400 before and after) and still no bytes: unavailable/content_sha256_mismatch, i.e. the digest catches it, not the guard. (3) 2 MiB file rewritten in place with the same length during the read (after the first 1 MiB chunk) + mtime restored -> GUARD DEFEATED, the buffer is a genuine mix of two revisions (mixed digest 88296cac..., requested 16d4332f...), and still no bytes: unavailable/content_sha256_mismatch. This is the decisive case: the guard's stated purpose ('refuse a buffer that may mix two revisions even if its digest looks self-consistent') cannot be tested by this buffer, because a buffer whose digest equals the requested digest IS the requested bytes. (4) truncate-and-rewrite to the same length -> no bytes, content_sha256_mismatch (size ends equal, so only the digest can decide). (5) write between the last read() and the post-stat (append of 9 bytes after the payload was fully read) -> refused changed_during_read even though the buffer in hand was byte-for-byte the requested version - the guard can only ADD refusals of correct buffers, it cannot widen what is accepted. Append-then-restore-to-original-size-and-mtime during the read -> bytes ARE returned, and they are exactly the requested version (verified: returned digest == requested digest), which is the correct outcome.
questions.evidence: RUN/evidence/b03_review_bytes.json scenarios same_size_overwrite_before_call, same_size_overwrite_with_mtime_restored (guard_defeated=true), mid_read_rewrite_same_size_mtime_restored (guard_defeated, mixed buffer, refused), truncate_and_rewrite_same_length, write_between_last_read_and_post_stat, mid_read_append_then_restore_original; the mutation M2_recheck_off shows the re-check is load-bearing for the reason LABEL only (it kills exactly test_r4b03_change_during_read_is_refused)

questions.question: Is the containment check correct at its edges? (root that is a textual prefix of another root, file path equal to a root path, case differences on Windows, root that is itself a symlink, junction/reparse point, path that does not exist yet)
questions.answer: Correct for six of the eight edges I measured, and WRONG for one real case (volume roots). Correct: textual-prefix sibling (root .../companies vs file .../companies_x/2025.pdf -> outside, because the comparison uses base + os.sep); file path equal to the root -> treated as inside and then refused not_regular_file (a directory is not a servable file); case differences on Windows -> inside in both directions (normcase lower-cases both sides, verified with an all-uppercase target AND an all-uppercase root); root that is itself a link -> inside, because realpath resolves BOTH sides (verified with a junction configured as the root); junction/reparse point INSIDE the root pointing outside -> correctly OUTSIDE and refused not_found BEFORE any read (junction resolved by realpath on Python 3.13/Windows - this is stronger than the author's symlink case, which skips on this host); non-existent path under a root -> inside and then read_failed, and a non-existent path under an in-root junction escape -> correctly outside. WRONG: a root configured as a VOLUME ROOT ('C:\', 'D:\', a mapped 'Z:\') refuses EVERY file under it: os.path.realpath('C:\\') returns 'C:\\' with its trailing separator preserved (realpath of an ordinary directory or of a UNC share root strips it), so base + os.sep becomes 'C:\\' and 'C:\Windows\win.ini'.startswith('C:\\') is False -> the entry point answers not_found/artifact_path_outside_allowed_root for a file that really is inside a configured root (finding B-VR03-02). End-to-end on this host the out-of-root-link property also holds at the SCAN layer: with an in-root junction to an outside directory the scanner did not index the file at all (resolve -> missing, 0 matches, empty debug_trace), so the bytes are refused twice over.
questions.evidence: RUN/evidence/b03_review_paths.json (realpath_semantics: 'C:\\' -> 'C:\\'; 14-row containment matrix; entrypoint::junction_escape -> not_found, bytes_leaked=false; entrypoint::hardlink_to_outside_bytes -> verified; entrypoint::drive_root_root -> not_found) and RUN/evidence/b03_review_junction.json (end-to-end junction fixture: resolve_status=missing, matches=0, bytes_leaked=false)

questions.question: Are the five-value claims real? Enumerate every failure the entry point can produce and check each is one of the five (and that no failure returns data).
questions.answer: Yes for the claim as scoped to refusals: every refusal is 'not_found' or 'unavailable' (two of the five), never a sixth value, and no refusal returns data. Complete enumeration from the code with what I measured: (1) locator outside the configured roots -> not_found + artifact_path_outside_allowed_root, zero reads [measured]; (2) budget already cancelled -> unavailable + cancelled [measured]; (3) stat() OSError (missing file, ACL denial, race) -> unavailable + read_failed + exception class name [FileNotFoundError measured; the ACL variant is the author's own registered non-claim]; (4) not a regular file (directory, device) -> unavailable + not_regular_file [measured]; (5) cloud placeholder attributes -> unavailable + placeholder_not_hydrated, no read, no hydration [the author's case plus my mutation M5_hydration_off which kills it]; (6) size over _CANDIDATE_BYTES_CAP at stat time -> unavailable + exceeds_candidate_cap [measured]; (7) take_candidate/charge budget stop -> unavailable + budget_exceeded (or cancelled if sticky) [measured]; (8) OSError while opening/reading -> unavailable + read_failed [path read from code, not separately forced]; (9) file grew past the cap DURING the read -> unavailable + exceeds_candidate_cap [read from code; the pre-check branch is the one I measured - both produce the same status/reason so the five-value claim is unaffected]; (10) stat() OSError after the read -> unavailable + read_failed [read from code]; (11) size or mtime changed -> unavailable + changed_during_read [measured]; (12) digest mismatch or an empty expected digest -> unavailable + content_sha256_mismatch [measured, including a handle with content_sha256='']. Non-contract outcomes exist only outside the refusal model: the success path returns status='verified' (not one of the five, see B-VR03-08), and a non-SourceHandle argument raises AttributeError instead of a contract refusal (resolve() type-checks its request, this entry point does not).

questions.question: Sample the B01 dispositions that landed in be2e4ed and f0aacbf: (i) does the author's own mutation harness really kill filter_off and x2_kind_only with the cases the author names? (ii) is CFG-08 complete for the boolean fields it claims to guard? (iii) is reusing the registered reason code artifact_path_outside_allowed_root for a SOURCE-file locator sound, or does it create taxonomy confusion?
questions.answer: (i) YES, exactly as recorded. I used the author's harness in its save/restore modes (never git checkout): baseline 9 passed; filter_off (removing the candidate-level reusable-root filter in _select_candidate) -> 2 failed / 7 passed, the failures being test_r4b01_resolver_set_matches_the_exported_policy and test_r4b01_empty_reusable_set_serves_nothing, i.e. precisely the two the disposition names (and NOT test_r4b01_explicit_false_is_not_reusable, which is the correction B-VR01-02 recorded); x2_kind_only (policy_2x._effective_reusable_2x back to the kind-only rule) -> 1 failed / 8 passed, the failure being test_r4b01_consumer_export_agrees_with_the_resolver_on_contradicting_flags, i.e. the new agreement case the disposition names. After restore both files were byte-identical to HEAD (sha256 resolver D69BC020.../policy_2x 4CEBC3BA...) and git status --short was empty. (ii) MOSTLY, with one hole. The two boolean fields of RootSpec are exactly read_only and reusable_for_filing (annotation scan of RootSpec and CatalogConfig), and CFG-08 refuses every wrong-typed value I fed it for both fields: quoted 'true'/'false', int 1/0 - all CatalogConfigError. YAML 1.1 spellings yes/no are real booleans and are admitted, which is correct. The hole: read_only: null. CFG-08's own docstring and the disposition say 'boolean or null, else CatalogConfigError', and _require_boolean deliberately lets null through - but RootSpec.__post_init__ (models.py:148) then raises a raw TypeError('read_only must be a boolean'), not a CatalogConfigError (reusable_for_filing: null is fine because it is annotated bool | None). So a config error escapes as an unhandled exception type, and the shipped case only covers two of the four directions (it tests reusable_for_filing: "false" and read_only: "true"). Finding B-VR03-03. (iii) The STATUS is contract-correct but the CODE is a taxonomy borrow, and it does create confusion that a future reader would hit. operation-contract.md:79 puts an out-of-bounds locator under not_found explicitly, so not_found is right. But artifact_path_outside_allowed_root is registered in observability.py inside the ARTIFACT family (:169 'artifact = "artifact"'; :183 'artifact - artifact schema/hash/binding/status + path-policy checks'; :239 maps the code to ('artifact',)) and its original emitter is artifact_handle.validate_artifact (:126-132), where the subject is a DERIVED artifact row's path under derived_dir - a different object class from a SOURCE document locator. Meanwhile the eight other reason codes this same entry point returns (content_sha256_mismatch, placeholder_not_hydrated, changed_during_read, read_failed, not_regular_file, exceeds_candidate_cap, budget_exceeded, cancelled) are not registered at all (measured against observability.REASONS), so the entry point's taxonomy is one borrowed artifact-family code plus eight invisible ones: family-level aggregation will file source-locator refusals under 'artifact'. The borrow was forced (F10/scope keeps observability.py out of the allowed set) and is documented at the emission site and in F-B01-9, so I record it as an accepted-with-action P2 rather than a blocker (finding B-VR03-05).

findings.claim: The public keyword expected_content_sha256 lets a caller redefine which version is being verified, and the result is then internally inconsistent: it carries the HANDLE's document_id together with ANOTHER version's bytes and digest, with status='verified', bytes_source='handle'. The entry point's own contract ('the bytes handed to a consumer must be the verified version's bytes', where the version is the handle's content_sha256) does not hold for that call form, and the parameter is neither documented in the docstring nor covered by any acceptance case.
findings.evidence: Measured (RUN/evidence/b03_review_bytes.json caller_supplied_foreign_digest): handle.content_sha256 = 5528ff0b36460ed1..., handle.document_id = urn:company-wiki:document:sha256:5528ff0b..., caller passes expected_content_sha256 = 3faa0bf24ac5761b... with the file holding those bytes; result: ok=True, status='verified', bytes_source='handle', byte_size=32, result.document_id = ...:5528ff0b... (the handle's), result.content_sha256 = 3faa0bf2..., data digest = 3faa0bf2.... So a (document_id, version) pair is returned that no catalog row asserts. The SAME parameter name already exists in this package with the OPPOSITE semantics: ReadOnlyCatalogReader.resolve_handle returns None when expected_content_sha256 != the document's content_sha ('# fail closed: bytes drifted from the claim', reader.py:338-342) and bundle() does the same (:367-371) - and that is the call form the run itself cites as the dereference API (findings.md F-B04-1). grep shows no product caller of read_verified_bytes yet and no test that passes the parameter, so the exposure today is zero call sites - which is exactly why this is P1 and not P0: it becomes wrong-bytes-served the moment B07 wires a consumer that pins a version by digest.
findings.impact: The step's central guarantee is caller-defeatable through an undocumented parameter whose name means the opposite of what it did everywhere else in the package. A consumer that asks for 'version X of document D' can be handed version Y's bytes labelled with D's document_id and status 'verified', and the result gives it no way to notice (both identity fields look authoritative).
findings.required_action: Bind the parameter to the handle before reading (refuse, or return a distinct status/reason, unless expected_content_sha256 is None or equals handle.content_sha256 - mirroring reader.resolve_handle's fail-closed rule), or make the override explicit in the result (a dedicated reason/field plus the digest actually used, and document_id reflecting the digest), and document the parameter in the docstring. Add acceptance cases for both the matching and the mismatching override. If the intended semantics is genuinely 'the caller defines the version', that decision belongs in the design and must say what document_id then means.

findings.claim: _inside_configured_roots rejects every file under a root that is a VOLUME ROOT (C:\, D:\, a mapped Z:\). os.path.realpath preserves the trailing separator for a drive root ('C:\\' -> 'C:\\'), so the check compares against base + os.sep == 'C:\\' and no real path can ever match; the entry point then answers not_found/artifact_path_outside_allowed_root for a locator that IS inside the configured root.
findings.evidence: Measured (RUN/evidence/b03_review_paths.json): realpath_semantics['C:\\'] = 'C:\\' (while an ordinary directory and a UNC share root both lose the trailing separator: 'C:\\Users\\' -> 'C:\\Users', '\\\\localhost\\C$\\' -> matched); containment::drive_root_root ('C:\\Users' under root 'C:\\') -> inside=false; containment::drive_root_file ('C:\\Windows\\win.ini') -> inside=false; entrypoint::drive_root_root -> status='not_found', reason='artifact_path_outside_allowed_root', refused before reading. RootSpec/load_catalog_config accept such a root without complaint (path is absolute and exists). Configs with a trailing separator ('...\\companies\\') and UNC roots are unaffected.
findings.impact: A plausible configuration (one volume registered as a root - e.g. an archive drive holding filings) makes the byte gate unusable for every file under it, and the reason code tells the operator the path is outside the allowed roots, which is the opposite of the truth. Fail-closed, so no wrong bytes, but the step's read path silently stops working for that root.
findings.required_action: Normalise the root before comparing (strip a trailing os.sep unless the root is exactly a drive/UNC root, or compare with os.path.commonpath / Path.is_relative_to), and add a containment case for a volume-root root (and for a trailing-separator root) to the acceptance or a probe.

findings.claim: CFG-08's declared rule ('a boolean or null, otherwise CatalogConfigError') is not honoured for read_only: an explicit YAML null passes the new admission check and then raises a raw TypeError from RootSpec.__post_init__ ('read_only must be a boolean') instead of the fail-closed CatalogConfigError the admission point is supposed to produce. The new acceptance case does not cover the null form.
findings.evidence: RUN/evidence/b03_review_cfg08.json: 17 generated configs through the real load_catalog_config. read_only: "true"/"false"/1/0 and reusable_for_filing: "false"/"true"/1/0 are all refused with CatalogConfigError (CFG-08 works for wrong TYPES in both fields, both directions); reusable_for_filing: <null> is admitted (annotated bool | None); read_only: <null> is ADMITTED by _require_boolean (config.py:52-65 explicitly allows None) and then raises TypeError from models.py:148 -> traceback captured in b03_review_cfg08_null.py (config.py:151 RootSpec(...) -> models.py:148). The shipped case test_r4b01_quoted_boolean_is_refused_by_the_admission_point builds one literal per field ('"false"' and '"true"' respectively), so neither the null form nor the string-int forms are pinned.
findings.impact: A plain config typo (an empty value, or a templating engine emitting an empty string for read_only) escapes as an unhandled TypeError instead of the config error callers catch, so config_doctor/CLI paths that handle CatalogConfigError will crash instead of reporting. Small, but it is exactly the admission-contract claim the disposition makes for B-VR01-04.
findings.required_action: Either refuse null for read_only with CatalogConfigError (RootSpec annotates only the field as bool, unlike reusable_for_filing's bool | None) or default it to True; extend the CFG-08 case to the null form for both fields. If null must stay admitted, RootSpec.__post_init__ should raise CatalogConfigError rather than TypeError so the admission point keeps a single error type.

findings.claim: The claimed sticky cancellation ('cancellation -> cancelled (sticky)', implementation record rule R6: 'a mid-read cancellation never returns bytes') is false in one reachable window: the read loop checks budget.cancelled only BEFORE each read(), and there is no guard after the loop, so a cancellation that lands inside the read() returning b'' is not observed and the entry point returns status='verified' with bytes while budget.cancelled is True. The B02 sibling _select_candidate was given a post-walk guard for exactly this class after two review rounds; the new B03 function has none.
findings.evidence: Deterministic construction (RUN/evidence/b03_review_bytes.json cancel_inside_final_read): with a wrapped file object that cancels the injected _ReadBudget inside the read call that returns b'', the result is status='verified', reason='', data present, byte_size=34, while budget.cancelled is True (contrast cancel_before_call -> unavailable/cancelled, which the author's case covers). Mutation M4_inloop_cancel_off (loop check removed) SURVIVES all 13 B03 cases, showing no case exercises mid-read cancellation at all. Code: resolver.py:380-394 (the only cancellation check is the loop head) vs resolver.py:1576-1577 (B02's tail guard 'if stop_status == "cancelled" or budget.cancelled'). Returned bytes are still the verified version, so this is a contract/consumer-semantics failure, not a wrong-bytes path.
findings.impact: A caller that cancels (shutdown, user abort, a shared per-request budget) can still be handed bytes after the cancellation, which the step's own rule table says never happens. The window is narrow and needs an injected budget and concurrent cancellation, and no product caller exists yet, so it does not block; but the same defect class already cost two B02 review rounds, which is why I rate it P2 rather than P3.
findings.required_action: Add the missing tail guard (mirror _select_candidate: after the read loop, refuse with unavailable/cancelled if budget.cancelled), and add the analogue of test_r4b02_mid_read_cancellation_returns_no_handle to the B03 file - a case that cancels during the read (a wrapped handle or a threaded cancel) so the mutant M4 no longer survives.

findings.claim: The out-of-root refusal borrows artifact_path_outside_allowed_root, an ARTIFACT-family code, for a SOURCE-document locator, while the eight other reason codes this same entry point returns are unregistered - so the taxonomy is inconsistent and family-level reporting will misclassify source-locator refusals as artifact problems.
findings.evidence: observability.py:102 (the code's text), :169 ('artifact = "artifact"'), :183 (family comment 'artifact - artifact schema/hash/binding/status + path-policy checks'), :239 (the code is mapped to the ('artifact',) family); the original emitter is artifact_handle.validate_artifact (:126-132, rejecting a DERIVED artifact row's path against derived_dir). New emitter resolver.py:1770 applies it to a SOURCE document's canonical_path. Registration check against observability.REASONS: artifact_path_outside_allowed_root = REGISTERED; content_sha256_mismatch, placeholder_not_hydrated, changed_during_read, read_failed, not_regular_file, exceeds_candidate_cap, budget_exceeded, cancelled = NOT registered (the FC-1301 gate only scans reason="..." keyword literals, which the resolver's positional returns do not use - the author registers this gap in F-B01-9 while also relying on it). The STATUS is right per the contract: operation-contract.md:79 lists the out-of-bounds locator under not_found.
findings.impact: A future reader (or a metrics rollup keyed on the taxonomy family) sees source-file path violations counted as artifact violations, and cannot see the eight real read-path reasons at all. The borrow is documented at the emission site, but the registry itself still asserts the artifact meaning.
findings.required_action: Keep the code for now (the file-scope constraint is real) but record the borrow in the registry's own words (a comment next to observability.py:102/:239 is outside B's file scope, so minimally ensure the follow-up package - widen the taxonomy scan and register the read-path codes - explicitly owns re-homing this code or adding a source-scoped twin), and note in the B03 record that the plan's working name path_outside_configured_roots is what the reader should expect once that package lands.

findings.claim: The size+mtime re-check is presented as the mechanism that stops a buffer mixing two revisions ('refuse it even if the digest of what we happened to read looks right'), but it is not load-bearing for integrity: it can be defeated with os.utime (measured) and, when it fires, the digest gate would have refused the buffer anyway - while it also refuses buffers that are byte-for-byte correct. Its real value is diagnostic precision (changed_during_read vs content_sha256_mismatch). Relatedly, read_at is stamped before Path.open, so the field a consumer reads as 'when these bytes were observed' is the request time.
findings.evidence: RUN/evidence/b03_review_bytes.json: same_size_overwrite_with_mtime_restored (guard_defeated=true, mtime_ns identical 1789251840518958400, refusal comes from content_sha256_mismatch); mid_read_rewrite_same_size_mtime_restored (2 MiB, mixed buffer digest 88296cac... vs requested 16d4332f..., refused by the digest); write_between_last_read_and_post_stat (refused changed_during_read although the buffer was exactly the requested version); mutation M2_recheck_off is killed by exactly one case, which asserts the reason LABEL. resolver.py:1756 sets read_at before the read at :1777.
findings.impact: The commit message and the code comment justify the re-stat with a power it does not have, which invites a future reader to treat it as the guarantee (and to weaken the digest gate reasoning 'the size check covers it'). The direction of the mistake is safe (fail-closed), so this is a wording/role issue, not a defect.
findings.required_action: Reword the resolver comment and the corresponding run-record sentence to say what the re-check is for (precise refusal labelling and an explicit signal that the file moved under the reader) and state that the digest comparison is the integrity mechanism; optionally note read_at's semantics (request-entry timestamp) or rename the field.

findings.claim: Containment is enforced on NAMES, not on file objects, and the check is separated from the open by a TOCTOU window: a hardlink whose other name is outside the root is served, and _inside_configured_roots resolves the realpath while _read_verified_bytes opens the original (unresolved) path, so a link swapped in between is not seen by the check. Neither can produce wrong bytes, because the digest gate still applies to whatever is read.
findings.evidence: entrypoint::hardlink_to_outside_bytes (RUN/evidence/b03_review_paths.json): the hardlink is inside the root, realpath does not resolve hardlinks, the bytes come from a file whose other name lives outside the root -> status='verified'. Code: _inside_configured_roots (:328-340) computes os.path.realpath, _read_verified_bytes (:359-360, :380) stats and opens the ORIGINAL path. The junction matrix shows realpath DOES resolve junctions/symlinks, so the name-based check catches the link cases it is meant to catch; only hardlinks and the swap window remain.
findings.impact: A reader could take 'the locator resolves outside the configured roots -> not_found' as a file-identity guarantee, which it is not. Both residuals require write access inside a root and both are capped by the digest gate (the outside file must be byte-identical to the requested version), so the exposure is theoretical.
findings.required_action: Register both as accepted limitations of the read path in the B03 record (name-based containment; check-then-open window bounded by the digest gate), or close the window cheaply by opening the resolved target (which the check already computed) instead of the raw handle path.

findings.claim: The new entry point's own API surface is inconsistent with the contract vocabulary it claims to use: the success status is the bare literal 'verified' (not one of the five values, and not a module constant while both error values are), refusals encode 'no object' as bytes_source='' with no sentinel constant, and there is no isinstance guard on handle (resolve() type-checks its request and the constructor type-checks the catalog), so a misuse raises AttributeError instead of a contract refusal.
findings.evidence: resolver.py:1783 (status=status or 'verified'), :1788 (bytes_source=... if data is not None else ''), :1755 (expected = expected_content_sha256 or handle.content_sha256 dereferences the handle before any check); measured: non_handle_argument -> AttributeError("'NoneType' object has no attribute 'content_sha256'") (b03_review_bytes.json). The acceptance sweep asserts 'status in CONTRACT_ERRORS' for refusals only, so the mixed vocabulary is not pinned either way.
findings.impact: A consumer that switches on ByteReadResult.status and knows the five-value model has no documented success value to match, and the failure mode of a wrong argument type is a Python exception rather than a refused read - which is the opposite of the fail-explicitly discipline the step is built on.
findings.required_action: Export a success constant alongside B03_ERROR_* (or document that status is a free-form label with the five values used for refusals only), use a named sentinel for 'no bytes_source', and add the same isinstance(handle, SourceHandle) guard that resolve() has.

No product caller of read_verified_bytes exists anywhere in src/ or scripts/ (grep), so every consumer-side consequence in this record - including the P1 override finding and the cancellation window - is prospective: B07 is where the wiring lands. The production multi-root catalog (and any real drive-root/UNC root configuration) was not inspected; the containment findings come from synthetic configs built with the product's own CatalogConfig/RootSpec.

The controlled-snapshot search (question e) covered the company-wiki repository only; I did not search the revenue-forecast repo or the other consumer repos for a source-byte snapshot object, and I did not attempt to PROVE that no snapshot could exist on the write face - I read the write paths (canonical_writer/portfolio_promoter copy source bytes as part of import, which is the primary copy, not a snapshot).
